Findings.problem: The multi-hop daddr/paddr/nframes/nbytes wrappers do not constrain r at all. map only establishes inner.wf(), and read_inner only returns an invariant guard, so even the private exact getters do not give public callers a way to recover the mapping identity and size promised at construction.
Findings.key_premise: The multi-hop daddr/paddr/nframes/nbytes wrappers do not constrain r at all. map only establishes inner.wf(), and read_inner only returns an invariant guard, so even the private exact getters do not give public callers a way to recover the mapping identity and size promised at construction.
Findings.suggestion: Introduce a public abstract mapping descriptor tied to the guarded state, preserving concurrency semantics. On successful map relate it to the input segment; have public address/size getters return its corresponding fields. If public inner mutation prevents stable identity, specify values from an explicit read snapshot instead. Do not equate mutable protected data with a permanently fixed value without an invariant.

Findings.problem: Both VmIo postconditions are disabled, so read/write expose no result or final state guarantees for the exec cursor and both tracked mutable owners, including success. The trait explicitly promises no short reads/writes, but callers cannot recover validity or ownership for a second call.

Findings.suggestion: Prove and enable the read/write contracts, covering cursor, owner and memory effects in both Ok and Err arms. Preserve partial-copy/error semantics accurately. The supplied FallibleVmRead/Write trait declarations themselves have no contracts, so inherited dependency guarantees must first be made available at those declarations (outside reporting scope); do not patch individual impl ensures and assume generic trait callers see them.

Findings.problem: read_requires excludes every kernel buffer, and write_requires has the same restriction, although VmIo supports slice-backed kernel readers/writers converted with to_fallible. A disjoint stack/heap byte buffer cannot be used for an ordinary DMA copy despite satisfying real ownership and non-overlap obligations.

Findings.suggestion: Replace exclusion of the entire kernel interval with the needed disjointness against the actual mapped transfer range, exposed through a sound mapping model or permission protocol. Preserve validity, Some(ReadView/WriteView), initialization and ownership requirements. Do not remove necessary alias restrictions.

Findings.quoted_evidence:
/// Returns a reader to read data from it.
            reader_perm@.has_read_view(),
            r.wf(reader_perm@),
            KERNEL_BASE_VADDR <= r.cursor.range@.start,
            r.cursor.range@.end <= KERNEL_END_VADDR,
Findings.problem: reader/writer promise access to this mapping but expose only arbitrary kernel-range validity (writer even omits those bounds), with no starting address or extent tied to the mapping. reader also drops reader_inner’s read_view_initialized guarantee, preventing the next natural write call that requires an initialized read view.

Findings.suggestion: Tie each returned cursor and tracked owner range to a sound snapshot of this mapping, expose full initial remain/avail, and propagate reader_perm@.read_view_initialized(). Strengthen reader_inner/writer_inner to relate their result ranges to this@.data.segment, then carry the relation through public wrappers.
